newsitem.title: USA: US debt managers limit duration exposure Apr 1 wk.
newsitem.headline: US debt managers limit duration exposure Apr 1 wk.

text.p: Money managers maintained stable portfolio structures in U.S. debt markets last week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"In recent prior weeks, money managers had shortened up duration exposure and also raised some cash," the report said.
"Portfolio structures are currently short duration exposure. Cash positions are still relatively lean given duration structure," it said.
In the week ended April 1, duration bogey rose to 4.24 from 4.14 on an arithmetic basis and remained steady at 4.70 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index fell to 4.66 from 4.72 on an arithmetic basis. It slipped to 5.00 from 5.01 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio in the past week held on to 7.02 percent.
Sixteen percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, unchanged from the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was unchanged at 5.75.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
